p: What makes this branch a bit different is where it sits. Rushden Lakes isn't your usual out-of-town retail park plonked in a car park. It was built beside a string of former gravel pits in the Nene Valley, and the water, wildlife and walking paths are right there on the doorstep, which gives you a ready-made way to balance a high-energy session with something slower.

The Wildlife Trust's Nene Wetlands visitor centre sits at the lakes, and it's a good place to find out what lives in the reserve around you. From there the paths lead out along the water and towards the River Nene, so even a short loop gives kids the chance to spot swans, ducks and the odd heron while their legs recover. Bring wellies or old trainers if it's been wet, as the paths beyond the shops can get muddy.

If you've got a bigger day planned, Irchester Country Park is a short drive away towards Wellingborough, with woodland trails and play areas, and the old towns of Higham Ferrers and Rushden are right next door for a wander and a bite to eat.

A good rhythm for a family day goes something like this: book a morning bounce while everyone's fresh, grab lunch at one of the places around the lakes, then head outdoors for an hour by the water. Teenagers may prefer to stay and mooch round the shops, which is fine too.

As with any trampoline park, empty pockets before jumping, wear clothes you can stretch in, and keep water handy. Weekends and school holidays bring the biggest crowds to the whole site, so earlier slots tend to be easier on everyone.
